title: $f^*\circ p_Y^*\cong p_X^*$ is monoidal
statement:
The natural isomorphism $f^*\circ p_Y^*\cong p_X^*$ of
[def-sfb-pullback-from-point-comp-iso] is monoidal. That is, it is compatible
with the unit and tensor comparison isomorphisms of the strong monoidal
functors $f^*\circ p_Y^*$ and $p_X^*$, for the tensor products of
[sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor].

proof.text: Work with abelian sheaves and their tensor product over $\mathbf Z$, not their cartesian product. Put $a=\pi_Y$, $h=a\circ f=\pi_X$, $A=a^*$, $B=f^*$, $U=a_*$, $V=f_*$, $H=h^*$ and $K=h_*$. By [def-sfb-finite-upper-star-monoidal] the three pullbacks are strong monoidal for the tensor product of [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. By [lem-sfb-finite-monoidal-adjunction] the units and counits of $A\dashv U$, $B\dashv V$ and $H\dashv K$ are monoidal natural transformations. These statements apply to arbitrary scheme morphisms, so apply to $f,a,h$ without properness or finiteness assumptions.

source.place: second paragraph: the adjunctions are monoidal; fix all three adjunctions and the tensor convention

proof.text:
Here are the elementary monoidal diagram calculations used below. Write $\mu^F_{M,N}:FM\otimes FN\to F(M\otimes N)$ and $e^F:\mathbf1\to F\mathbf1$. For monoidal $s:F\to G$ and $t:G\to J$,
$$ (t s)_{M\otimes N}\mu^F=t_{M\otimes N}\mu^G(s_M\otimes s_N)=\mu^J(t_M\otimes t_N)(s_M\otimes s_N)=\mu^J((t s)_M\otimes(t s)_N),\qquad (t s)_{\mathbf1}e^F=e^J. $$
Thus their composite is monoidal. Postcomposition by a lax monoidal functor $T$ preserves these equations by naturality of $\mu^T,e^T$ and $\mu^{TF}=T(\mu^F)\mu^T$, $e^{TF}=T(e^F)e^T$. Precomposition by a lax monoidal $S$ preserves them by naturality of $s$ at $\mu^S,e^S$ and $\mu^{FS}=F(\mu^S)\mu^F$, $e^{FS}=F(e^S)e^F$. If $s$ is invertible, multiplying its tensor equation by $s^{-1}_{M\otimes N}$ and by $s_M^{-1}\otimes s_N^{-1}$ gives the equation for $s^{-1}$; multiplying its unit equation gives its unit equation. These are direct computations with the definitions, not additional geometric lemmas.

source.place: second paragraph, last sentence: write out the monoidal transformation calculus instead of invoking an uncited mate theorem

proof.text: Set $L=BA$ and $R=UV$. The composite adjunction $L\dashv R$ is obtained by the two successive Hom bijections. If $u^A,v^A$ and $u^B,v^B$ denote the units and counits, its unit at $F$ is $u_F=U(u^B_{AF})\circ u^A_F$ and its counit at $G$ is $v_G=v^B_G\circ B(v^A_{VG})$. Its strong/lax structures are the composite ones. Each displayed transformation is a composite of whiskered monoidal units or counits from step 1, so the calculations of step 2 prove that $u$ and $v$ are monoidal. In particular this is a monoidal adjunction with exactly the composite structures, not merely with some isomorphic structures. The Hom bijections and the displayed unit/counit also follow directly from the adjunction of [def-sfb-finite-upper-lower-star-adjunction].

source.place: second paragraph: the adjunction for the composite pullback; its unit and counit written explicitly

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-pushforward-comp-monoidal] with $g=a$ and coefficient category $\Ab$: the canonical isomorphism $c:R=UV\xrightarrow{\sim}K$, induced by $(W\times_{\Spec\mathbf Z}Y)\times_YX\cong W\times_{\Spec\mathbf Z}X$, is monoidal. Hence $c^{-1}:K\to R$ is monoidal by step 2. Write $u^H$ for the unit of $H\dashv K$. The adjoint comparison $b:L\to H$ inverse to the canonical composition isomorphism $H\to L$ has the explicit formula
$$ b_F=v_{HF}\circ L(c^{-1}_{HF})\circ L(u^H_F). $$
Indeed the first map inserts $F\to KHF$, the second replaces $K$ by $R$, and the last evaluates $LRHF\to HF$; this is the defining two-adjunction transpose of $c^{-1}$. Its inverse is the transpose of $c$ in the other direction: cancellation follows from $cc^{-1}=1$, naturality, and the two triangle identities. In particular the formula is for $L\to H$, the direction used in [def-sfb-pullback-from-point-comp-iso]. Each of the three factors is monoidal: respectively the unit of $H\dashv K$ whiskered by $L$, $c^{-1}$ whiskered by $L,H$, and the composite-adjunction counit whiskered by $H$. Step 2 therefore proves both monoidal equations for $b$. This supplies the mate argument in the blueprint rather than assuming it as a new lemma.

source.place: second paragraph: monoidal pushforward composition and its conjugate; use the inverse right-adjoint map for the comparison L to H

proof.text: The functor $p^*$ is strong monoidal by [lem-sfb-point-upper-star-braided]. Precompose $b$ with $p^*$; step 2 gives a monoidal comparison $BAp^*\to Hp^*$. The functors in [def-sfb-upper-star-from-point] are $p_Y^*=Ap^*$ and $p_X^*=\pi_X^*p^*$. By [def-sfb-pullback-from-point-comp-iso] the comparison in the statement is precisely this whiskered map, with the reassociation of composites and $h=\pi_X$. The reassociation has identity components and is monoidal: expanding either parenthesization gives the same tensor comparison $BA(\mu^{p^*})\circ B(\mu^A)\circ\mu^B$ and the same unit comparison $BA(e^{p^*})\circ B(e^A)\circ e^B$. The equality $h=\pi_X$ identifies the functor and its specified monoidal structure simultaneously, so its equality isomorphism is monoidal by substitution. Composing these maps gives the unit and tensor compatibility of $f^*p_Y^*\cong p_X^*$, as required.
